venues.name: Ellerman House
venues.note: A private cliff-side mansion above the Atlantic, run as a home with one of Africa's great art and wine cellars.
credentials: Travel + Leisure World's Best Awards 2024, Best City Hotel in Africa

venues.name: Mount Nelson, A Belmond Hotel
venues.note: The Pink Lady, Cape Town's grande dame since 1899, in nine acres of gardens below Table Mountain.
credentials: World's 50 Best Hotels 2024 (No. 28), Best Hotel in Africa

venues.name: One&Only Cape Town
venues.note: A marina-side resort with Table Mountain framed in the glass and a private spa island of its own.
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Choice Awards 2024

venues.name: The Silo Hotel
venues.note: A converted grain silo crowned with faceted glass, sitting atop the Zeitz MOCAA contemporary-art museum.
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Choice Awards

venues.name: Delaire Graff Lodge
venues.note: Laurence Graff's jewel of a wine estate on the Helshoogte Pass, art, diamonds and vineyards at altitude.

venues.name: Cape Grace, A Fairmont Managed Hotel
venues.note: A warm, quietly grand harbour house on its own quay, with one of the city's finest whisky bars.
credentials: Travel + Leisure World's Best Awards 2024 (Top City Hotels in Africa, No. 3)

venues.name: The Cellars-Hohenort
venues.note: A country-house hotel in nine acres of Constantia gardens, the calm, green, old-Cape antidote to the city.

venues.name: The Twelve Apostles Hotel and Spa
venues.note: A sea-facing house between mountain and Atlantic on the scenic road to Camps Bay, remote calm, minutes from town.
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller Triple Crown (Hot List, Gold List & Readers' Choice)
Red Carnation Hotels, TripAdvisor Hall of Fame

venues.name: Steenberg Hotel & Spa
venues.note: The Cape's oldest wine farm turned polished retreat, vineyards, a golf course and Cape Dutch calm.

venues.name: La Residence
venues.note: The Royal Portfolio's flamboyant, art-filled manor on a private vine-and-olive estate in the valley.
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice Awards 2024 (Top 15 Hotels in South Africa)

venues.name: Leeu House
venues.note: An intimate boutique house in the heart of Franschhoek village, art, gardens and the main street at the door.

venues.name: Le Quartier Français
venues.note: A legendary village inn reborn, the beating heart of Franschhoek's dining-and-village life.

venues.name: Akademie Street Boutique Hotel
venues.note: A cluster of restored village cottages and suites with private pools, run with real warmth.

venues.name: Taj Cape Town
venues.note: The old Reserve Bank turned grand city hotel, and the address that speaks Hindi at the door.

venues.name: Cape Cadogan Boutique Hotel
venues.note: A restored Georgian-and-Victorian townhouse on a leafy Gardens street, a calm, characterful city base.
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice Awards (Best Hotels in Africa, No. 5)

venues.name: La Colombe
venues.note: Cape Town's most celebrated kitchen, a treehouse-like room above Silvermist, and Africa's benchmark for fine dining.
credentials: World's 50 Best Restaurants No. 49 (2024), Best Restaurant in Africa

venues.name: FYN
venues.note: Japanese precision married to South African produce, the only stand-alone African restaurant in Relais & Châteaux.
credentials: Eat Out Restaurant of the Year & Three Stars (2026)

venues.name: Salsify at the Roundhouse
venues.note: Chef Ryan Cole's seasonal cooking in a historic hunting lodge, with the Atlantic sweeping below.
credentials: Eat Out Restaurant of the Year & Three Stars (2025)

venues.name: La Petite Colombe
venues.note: La Colombe's Winelands sibling at Leeu Estates, theatrical tasting menus among the vines.

venues.name: Pier
venues.note: Waterside fine dining with table-side theatre and the ocean's finest produce at its centre.

venues.name: Salon
venues.note: An intimate, ambitious tasting-menu room that climbed to the very top of the Cape's rankings.

venues.name: Dusk
venues.note: A Stellenbosch tasting-menu room that arrived at three stars almost fully formed.

venues.name: Wolfgat
venues.note: Kobus van der Merwe's veldkos, foraged 'field food' from the strandveld, in a fisherman's cottage by the sea.
credentials: World Restaurant Awards, Restaurant of the Year (inaugural)

venues.name: Beyond
venues.note: Buitenverwachting's elegant estate restaurant, refined cooking among the Constantia vines.

venues.name: Chefs Warehouse at Beau Constantia
venues.note: Small tapas-style plates on a mountainside deck with one of the Cape's great views.

venues.name: Foxcroft
venues.note: Refined 'soigné' cooking in an approachable, everyday-elegant Constantia room.

venues.name: Ouzeri
venues.note: Nic Charalambous's modern Greek-Cypriot, family recipes, Cape produce, and a buzzing Wale Street room.

venues.name: The Pot Luck Club
venues.note: Luke Dale Roberts's tapas-and-views room atop the Old Biscuit Mill, small plates, big city panorama.

venues.name: The Waterside
venues.note: Waterside fine dining with a light, produce-led hand and harbour calm.

venues.name: Rust en Vrede
venues.note: A landmark wine-estate restaurant in a 300-year-old cellar, polished cooking and revered reds.

venues.name: Epice
venues.note: A spice-led tasting menu in the village, fragrant, considered, and quietly excellent.

venues.name: Protégé
venues.note: A young-guns village kitchen doing sharp, seasonal cooking without ceremony.

venues.name: MERTIA
venues.note: A Stellenbosch tasting room that rose to the very top, precise, ingredient-led, personal.

venues.name: Belly of the Beast
venues.note: One lunch, one dinner, no menu, a daily set feast of local, sustainable produce, cooked with heart.

venues.name: Galjoen
venues.note: Sustainably caught South African seafood from the Belly of the Beast team, sea-to-table and quietly serious.

venues.name: The Test Kitchen Fledgelings
venues.note: Luke Dale Roberts's learning kitchen, training the next generation while cooking at a starred level.

venues.name: Upper Union
venues.note: An intimate neighbourhood room punching well above its size, on the slopes of the City Bowl.

venues.name: Chefs Warehouse at Tintswalo Atlantic
venues.note: Small plates at the water's edge below the Twelve Apostles, cooking and coastline in equal measure.

venues.name: Ëlgr
venues.note: A pared-back, produce-first tasting room in the city, quiet, precise, ingredient-led.

venues.name: The Red Room by Chefs Warehouse
venues.note: The Chefs Warehouse group's intimate city room, small, sharing-led plates done with real polish.

venues.name: Reverie Social Table
venues.note: A communal-table neighbourhood favourite where you eat what the chef feels like cooking.

venues.name: Chefs Warehouse at Maison
venues.note: Small plates and vineyard views at a Franschhoek wine estate, relaxed, generous, sharing-led.

venues.name: Le Coin Français
venues.note: Classic French technique in the village, from a chef with a devoted following.

venues.name: Amura
venues.note: Ángel León's Cape Town debut at the Mount Nelson, the 'chef of the sea', translated to the Atlantic.

venues.name: Table Mountain
venues.note: The flat-topped mountain the whole city arranges itself around, take the rotating cable car up, and walk the summit while the Cape falls away on every side.

venues.name: Robben Island
venues.note: The island where Nelson Mandela was held for eighteen years, reached by ferry from the Waterfront and shown, movingly, by former prisoners themselves.

venues.name: Cape of Good Hope & Cape Point
venues.note: The dramatic, wind-carved southern tip of the peninsula, a funicular to the old lighthouse, cliffs plunging to two oceans, and the great sweep of the Cape at its wildest.

venues.name: Kirstenbosch National Botanical Garden
venues.note: One of the world's great botanical gardens, set against the eastern slopes of Table Mountain, given over to the Cape's own fynbos and a treetop canopy walkway.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Cape Floral Region Protected Areas

venues.name: The Cape Winelands
venues.note: Stellenbosch and Franschhoek, Cape Dutch estates among the oldest in the New World, an easy hour from the city, best taken slowly over lunch and a tasting.

venues.name: Groot Constantia
venues.note: South Africa's oldest wine estate, producing since 1685, a manor-house museum, historic cellars and a tasting of the sweet Constantia wines once shipped to Europe's courts.
credentials: Oldest wine estate in South Africa (est. 1685)

venues.name: Zeitz MOCAA
venues.note: The largest museum of contemporary African art, carved from a 1920s grain silo by Thomas Heatherwick, the continent's cultural landmark, and its most photographed interior.
credentials: Largest museum of contemporary African art in the world

venues.name: Boulders Beach penguins
venues.note: A sheltered cove at Simon's Town where a colony of African penguins nests among the granite boulders, boardwalks bring you within arm's reach, without disturbing them.

venues.name: Chapman's Peak Drive
venues.note: One of the most beautiful coast roads on earth, a hundred and fourteen curves cut into the cliff face between Hout Bay and Noordhoek, the Atlantic straight below.

venues.name: Bo-Kaap
venues.note: The candy-coloured Cape Malay quarter on the slopes of Signal Hill, cobbled streets, a living Muslim community, and the city's oldest surviving residential fabric.

venues.name: V&A Waterfront
venues.note: The working Victorian harbour reborn as the Cape's front room, the ferry to Robben Island, Zeitz MOCAA, the Two Oceans Aquarium and the best of the city's shopping, all on the water.

venues.name: Signal Hill & the Noon Gun
venues.note: The low ridge beside Lion's Head, where locals gather for sunset over the Atlantic, and where a cannon has been fired at noon, every day, since 1806.

venues.name: Lion's Head
venues.note: The city's most-loved climb, a spiralling path to a 360-degree summit above the sea, walked at dawn, at sunset, and by the light of the full moon.

venues.name: Cape Point Ostrich & Peninsula drive
venues.note: The full loop of the Cape Peninsula, Chapman's Peak, the Cape of Good Hope reserve, Simon's Town and Kalk Bay strung along one of the world's great day-drives.

venues.name: Constantia wine route
venues.note: The city's own vineyard belt, fifteen minutes from town, Groot Constantia, Klein Constantia and Buitenverwachting among leafy estates you can taste across in an afternoon.

venues.name: Two Oceans Aquarium
venues.note: A window onto the meeting of the cold Atlantic and warm Indian oceans, kelp forests, ragged-tooth sharks and a turtle rehabilitation programme, on the Waterfront's edge.

venues.name: The Silo Rooftop
venues.note: Drinks on the roof of the pillowed-glass Silo Hotel, above Zeitz MOCAA, the definitive Cape Town sundowner, Table Mountain on one side, the Atlantic on the other.
credentials: The Silo Hotel, Leading Hotels of the World; MICHELIN One Key (2025)

venues.name: Willaston Bar
venues.note: The Silo Hotel's double-height sixth-floor bar, teal banquettes, circular chandeliers and harbour views, the sheltered counterpart to the rooftop above.
credentials: Within The Silo Hotel, Leading Hotels of the World; The Royal Portfolio

venues.name: Cause | Effect Cocktail Kitchen
venues.note: Cape Town in a glass, fynbos, brandy and closed-loop, waterless technique from one of the country's most awarded bar teams, at the Waterfront and on Kloof Street.
credentials: World's 50 Best Bars, 50 Best Discovery selection
Home of the Cape Brandy Bar

venues.name: Art of Duplicity
venues.note: A password-only speakeasy in a Victorian warehouse, velvet, mahogany and one of the city's most inventive cocktail lists, found by those who know to look.
credentials: World's 50 Best Bars, 50 Best Discovery selection; ranked in the extended World's 50 Best Bars list

venues.name: Bascule Whisky, Wine & Cocktail Bar
venues.note: At Cape Grace on its own quay, more than four hundred whiskies and a marina-side terrace, the city's most serious address for a dram.
credentials: Within Cape Grace, A Fairmont Managed Hotel, MICHELIN Two Keys (2025)

venues.name: Ellerman House bar & terrace
venues.note: Sundowners on a cliff-side lawn above the Atlantic, drawn from a nine-thousand-bottle cellar of South Africa's finest, arguably the most beautiful sundowner in the city.
credentials: Within Ellerman House, Relais & Châteaux; MICHELIN Two Keys (2025)

venues.name: Chinchilla Rooftop
venues.note: Above the Camps Bay strip, the sun going down over the Atlantic, Lion's Head and the Twelve Apostles behind, cocktails and DJs as the beach empties.
credentials: Named among the world's best rooftop bars; Kove Collection

venues.name: Bree Street
venues.note: The city's coolest block after dark, wine bars, cocktail haunts and pavement tables strung along a heritage street, the natural place to begin a Cape Town night.
credentials: Cape Town's defining bar-and-restaurant street, City Bowl

venues.name: Long Street
venues.note: The Mother City's historic nightlife spine, Victorian balconies, live music and clubs running till dawn, loud, mixed and unpretentious.
credentials: Cape Town's most famous nightlife street, City Bowl
